Your goal is to produce a clear, concise, and well-structured document with descriptive headings and actionable explanations for each section.
Follow the outline below, but adapt as needed — add sections if relevant, and omit those that do not apply to this project.

Document Requirements

- Title the document "Repository Guidelines".
- Use Markdown headings (#, ##, etc.) for structure.
- Keep the document concise. 200-400 words is optimal.
- Keep explanations short, direct, and specific to this repository.
- Provide examples where helpful (commands, directory paths, naming patterns).
- Maintain a professional, instructional tone.

Recommended Sections

Project Structure & Module Organization

- Outline the project structure, including where the source code, tests, and assets are located.

Build, Test, and Development Commands

- Briefly explain what each command does.

Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Include any formatting or linting tools used.

Testing Guidelines

- Identify testing frameworks and coverage requirements.
- State test naming conventions and how to run tests.

Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Summarize commit message conventions found in the project’s Git history.
- Outline pull request requirements (descriptions, linked issues, screenshots, etc.).

(Optional) Add other sections if relevant, such as Security & Configuration Tips, Architecture Overview, or Agent-Specific Instructions.

+# Repository Guidelines
+
+## Project Structure & Module Organization
+- `platformio.ini` defines the single `ws-esp32s3` environment, pointing to the custom board JSON in `boards/` and configuring Arduino-on-ESP32 build flags, partition tables, and default upload speeds.
+- `src/main.cpp` is the sole entry point and orchestrates LVGL, RS485, settings management, and USB utilities; `src/settings_store.*` wraps NVS-backed persistence and must be kept in sync with UI globals.
+- `lib/` hosts project-local libraries (generated EEZ UI code, LVGL fork, IO drivers, etc.); keep each module self-contained under `lib/<name>/src` so PlatformIO’s Library Dependency Finder can link it automatically.
+- `firmware/eez/` contains .eez-project assets for editing UI flows, while `firmware/arduino/MEGA/` stores reference sketches for companion hardware; update these assets alongside firmware changes that affect layout or messaging.
+- Temporary build output lives under `.pio/`; hardware definitions and calibration data belong either in `boards/` or `mcpOmat*.zip` archives, not inside `src/`.
+
+## Build, Test, and Development Commands
+- `pio run` compiles the ESP32-S3 firmware using the configured flags; run it before committing to ensure reproducible binaries.
+- `pio run -t upload` flashes the board via USB CDC; ensure the correct port is selected or provide `-e ws-esp32s3 -p <port>` explicitly.
+- `pio device monitor -b 115200 --filter direct` opens the serial console with the required baud and RTS/DTR disabled, mirroring the settings in `platformio.ini`.
+- `pio run -t clean` resets the build tree when toggling LVGL buffers or board JSON values to avoid stale artifacts.
+- `pio check` runs PlatformIO’s static analysis (cppcheck/clang-tidy) and should stay warning-free for any modified files.
+
+## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
+- Use two-space indentation, brace-on-same-line, and wrap long argument lists similarly to `gfx->begin()` calls; avoid hard tabs.
+- Prefer camelCase for functions (`usbPoll`, `sendAllSettingsToArduino`) and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for `#define` constants or pin IDs.
+- Keep inline `static` helpers in the translation unit unless they need to be shared, and gate hardware-dependent code with the existing `USE_NATIVE_USB` or LVGL macros.
+- Favor `const`, `constexpr`, and `String`/`std::string` interop helpers over raw literals when touching settings or flow globals.
+- When adding a new module, expose declarations through a header in `src/` or `lib/<module>/src`, and include it explicitly rather than relying on Arduino’s auto-include.
+
+## Testing Guidelines
+- Add PlatformIO unit tests under `test/<feature>/test_main.cpp` using Unity, and run them with `pio test -e ws-esp32s3`; mock LVGL or RS485 dependencies where practical.
+- For integration checks, flash onto hardware and use `pio device monitor --echo` to validate RS485 commands, LVGL logging, and heap stats printed by `usbPoll()`.
+- Target tests toward `settings_store` logic, RS485 parsers, and any pure functions involved in EEZ state synchronization; document scenarios that still require manual validation (touch matrix, display timing, etc.).
+
+## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
+- Follow the existing short, imperative style from `git log` (e.g., `Serial Monitor + FullScreen Buf`): start with a verb, keep it under ~60 characters, and omit trailing punctuation.
+- Reference related issues or hardware tasks in the PR description, summarize functional changes, upload screenshots of UI updates, and paste relevant serial logs when altering comms behavior.
+- Detail how you validated the change (commands run, hardware used, EEZ project version) and call out required follow-up steps so reviewers can reproduce results quickly.
*** End Patch"]}

-- `pio run -t upload` flashes the board via USB CDC; ensure the correct port is selected or provide `-e ws-esp32s3 -p <port>` explicitly.
-- `pio device monitor -b 115200 --filter direct` opens the serial console with the required baud and RTS/DTR disabled, mirroring the settings in `platformio.ini`.
-- `pio run -t clean` resets the build tree when toggling LVGL buffers or board JSON values to avoid stale artifacts.
-- `pio check` runs PlatformIO’s static analysis (cppcheck/clang-tidy) and should stay warning-free for any modified files.

-## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
-- Use two-space indentation, brace-on-same-line, and wrap long argument lists similarly to `gfx->begin()` calls; avoid hard tabs.
-- Prefer camelCase for functions (`usbPoll`, `sendAllSettingsToArduino`) and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for `#define` constants or pin IDs.

-

-- For integration checks, flash onto hardware and use `pio device monitor --echo` to validate RS485 commands, LVGL logging, and heap stats printed by `usbPoll()`.

-

-- Follow the existing short, imperative style from `git log` (e.g., `Serial Monitor + FullScreen Buf`): start with a verb, keep it under ~60 characters, and omit trailing punctuation.

-- Detail how you validated the change (commands run, hardware used, EEZ project version) and call out required follow-up steps so reviewers can reproduce results quickly.
+# Repository Guidelines
+
+## Project Structure & Module Organization
+- `platformio.ini` describes the single `ws-esp32s3` environment and its custom board JSON in `boards/`.
+- `src/main.cpp` drives LVGL, RS485, and settings logic, while `src/settings_store.*` encapsulates NVS-backed persistence that must match UI globals.
+- `lib/` holds generated EEZ UI code, the LVGL fork, IO drivers, and other project-only modules; keep every library under `lib/<name>/src` so the dependency finder picks it up.
+- `firmware/eez/` stores editable `.eez-project` files, and `firmware/arduino/MEGA/` keeps supporting Arduino sketches for the external hardware; update these assets whenever protocol fields or layout change.
+- Build output lives inside `.pio/`; calibration JSON or archives (such as `mcpOmat*.zip`) belong outside `src/` to avoid polluting firmware sources.
+
+## Build, Test, and Development Commands
+- `pio run` builds the ESP32-S3 firmware; rerun after touching board settings, partitions, or LVGL flags.
+- `pio run -t upload -e ws-esp32s3 -p <port>` flashes via USB CDC; pass the COM port explicitly so uploads stay deterministic.
+- `pio device monitor -b 115200 --filter direct` mirrors the monitor configuration in `platformio.ini` (RTS/DTR low) and is the default way to inspect RS485/log output.
+- `pio run -t clean` clears stale artifacts before switching GT911, RGB, or partition parameters.
+- `pio check` enables cppcheck/clang-tidy; keep it warning-free for any modified files.
+
+## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
+- Use two-space indentation, braces on the same line, and wrap long parameter lists as shown in the LVGL buffer setup; avoid hard tabs.
+- Prefer camelCase for functions (`usbPoll`, `sendAllSettingsToArduino`), snake_case only when matching LVGL callbacks, and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for pins or compile-time flags.
+- Guard hardware-specific code with existing macros (`USE_NATIVE_USB`, `LV_USE_LOG`) and introduce `constexpr` identifiers rather than scattering literal values.
+- Keep helper declarations in headers (`settings_store.h`) and include them explicitly; do not rely on Arduino’s implicit prototypes.
+
+## Testing Guidelines
+- Place unit tests under `test/<feature>/test_main.cpp` using Unity assertions and run them with `pio test -e ws-esp32s3`.
+- Perform integration passes on real hardware: flash, then observe `usbPoll` responses through `pio device monitor --echo` while exercising RS485 packets; record any manual steps in the PR.
+- Focus automated coverage on deterministic logic (settings caching, RS485 parsing, UI flag updates) so only touch/timing paths require manual validation.
+
+## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
+- Follow the concise, imperative commit style already present in `git log` (for example, `Serial Monitor + FullScreen Buf`): single sentence, capitalized verb, no trailing punctuation.
+- Link related issues in PRs, summarize functional impact, list the build/test commands executed, and attach screenshots or serial logs whenever LVGL screens or protocol payloads change.
+- Mention the hardware revision, EEZ project touched, and any calibration files that must accompany the change so reviewers can reproduce results quickly.
*** End Patch"]}

+# Repository Guidelines
+
+## Project Structure & Module Organization
+- `platformio.ini` keeps the lone `ws-esp32s3` environment plus the matching board JSON in `boards/`.
+- `src/main.cpp` drives LVGL, RS485, and settings; `src/settings_store.*` hides NVS details and must mirror EEZ globals.
+- `lib/` contains generated UI code, the LVGL fork, IO helpers, etc.; keep each module in `lib/<name>/src` so PlatformIO links it automatically.
+- `firmware/eez/` stores `.eez-project` assets, while `firmware/arduino/MEGA/` holds supporting sketches; version these whenever protocol fields or layouts move.
+- Treat `.pio/` as disposable output and keep calibration JSON or archives (e.g., `mcpOmat*.zip`) outside `src/`.
+
+## Build, Test, and Development Commands
+- `pio run` builds the firmware; rerun after altering board options, partitions, or LVGL flags.
+- `pio run -t upload -e ws-esp32s3 -p <port>` flashes via USB CDC with explicit port selection.
+- `pio device monitor -b 115200 --filter direct` mirrors the serial monitor settings from `platformio.ini` and is the standard log/RS485 console.
+- `pio run -t clean` removes stale objects before switching pin maps or display timing constants.
+- `pio check` runs cppcheck/clang-tidy; keep it warning-free for touched files.
+
+## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
+- Use two-space indentation, braces on the same line, and wrap argument lists the same way as the LVGL buffer setup.
+- Prefer camelCase for functions or members, snake_case only for LVGL callback hooks, and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for pins, macros, or feature flags.
+- Introduce `constexpr` IDs instead of repeating literals, and guard hardware-specific blocks with existing macros (`USE_NATIVE_USB`, `LV_USE_LOG`, etc.).
+- Declare helpers inside headers such as `settings_store.h` and include them explicitly; do not rely on Arduino’s implicit prototypes.
+
+## Testing Guidelines
+- Place Unity-based unit tests under `test/<feature>/test_main.cpp` and run them with `pio test -e ws-esp32s3`.
+- Exercise integrations on hardware: flash, then observe `usbPoll` output with `pio device monitor --echo` while sending RS485 frames; describe manual steps in the PR.
+- Prioritize automated coverage for deterministic code (settings caching, RS485 parsing, UI flag bookkeeping) so only touch and timing paths stay manual.
+
+## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
+- Keep commits short, imperative, and capitalized like `Serial Monitor + FullScreen Buf`; avoid punctuation past the title.
+- PRs should link issues, summarize functional impact, list build/test commands, and attach screenshots or serial logs for UI or protocol changes.
